hypotheses.reasoning: event-processor crashes on the same message msg-149432 at offset 598134 every time it restarts (#156, #164, #174, #187) with RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded in expandReferences. After each restart it resumes at the committed offset 598134 (#160, #186, #216), so the consumer never gets past the bad record. The consumer group lag then climbs from 1518 to about 20k (#182 to #283) because nothing is processed. The crash loop is the poison message jamming the events.raw consumer. Restarts show backoff 10s to 80s (#157, #188).

The v3.10.1 rollout (build 97c3736) started at 12:43:10 and became ready at 12:43:41 (#116, #122). The first crash at 12:46:04 came about 2.5 minutes later, and the pod then ran v3.6.8 (#159), so the release may have changed how references are expanded and caused the recursion. But the same offset fails again on the older v3.6.8 build, which points to the message rather than the release. The release is a possible contributing factor, not the origin, so this is a lower-ranked alternative.

verdict.recommendedAction: Skip or quarantine offset 598134 (msg-149432) in events.raw, e.g. move it to a dead-letter topic or advance the consumer group past that offset, so event-processor can drain the backlog. Then fix expandReferences so it handles deeply nested or cyclic references (add a depth guard) and check whether v3.10.1 changed that code path. Also verify which build is actually running, since the pods came back on v3.6.8 after the 12:43 rollout of v3.10.1.
